title: Points, Lines, and Planes
seo_title: Points, Lines, and Planes Worksheet (Geometry, G-CO.A.1) | 100 Questions with Answers
standard_text: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment, based on the undefined notions of point, line, distance along a line, and distance around a circular arc.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on points, lines and planes: name rays and segments, collinear points, postulates, definitions and skew lines. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A ray is named endpoint first. Two lines meet in a point; two planes meet in a line.
key_sub: Collinear means on one line. Skew lines never meet and are not in one plane.
body_html:
How it works

Geometry starts with three words we do not define: point (a location), line (straight, goes on forever both ways) and plane (a flat surface that goes on forever). Everything else is defined from them.

  • Segment AB: two endpoints.
  • Ray AB: starts at A and goes on through B forever. Name the endpoint first.
  • Line AB: any two points on it name it.

Collinear points are on one line. Coplanar points are in one plane. Two lines meet in a point; two planes meet in a line.

Parallel lines are in one plane and never meet. Skew lines never meet and are not in one plane.

Example

Points A, B, C, D are on a line in that order. Is ray BC the same as ray BD?

Both rays start at B and go the same way, through C and on to D.

Answer: Yes, they are the same ray.

Example

In a box, edge AB is on the bottom front and edge CG is a back vertical edge. How are they related?

They never meet.

They point in different directions, so they are not parallel.

Answer: They are skew.

Common mistakes

  • Naming a ray with the endpoint second. Ray BA starts at B, not A.
  • Thinking any three points are collinear. Two points are always collinear, but a third may be off the line.
  • Calling skew lines parallel. Parallel lines must be in the same plane.
  • Counting line AB and line BA as two lines. They are the same line.

faq.q: What is the difference between a line, a ray and a segment?
faq.a: A line goes on forever in both directions. A ray has one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. A segment has two endpoints.

faq.q: What are undefined terms in geometry?
faq.a: Point, line and plane. They are described, not defined, and every other term is defined using them.
Lines that never intersect and are not in the same plane. They can only happen in three dimensions.

faq.q: How many points determine a line and a plane?
faq.a: Two points determine exactly one line. Three noncollinear points determine exactly one plane.

items.q: There are 4 points in a plane, and no three of them are collinear. How many lines can you draw through pairs of these points?
items.e: Each pair of points makes one line. The number of pairs is 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6. Do not count line AB and line BA twice.

items.q: There are 10 points in a plane, and no three of them are collinear. How many lines can you draw through pairs of these points?
items.e: Each pair of points makes one line. The number of pairs is 10 × 9 ÷ 2 = 45. Do not count line AB and line BA twice.

items.q: 6 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
items.e: Rays that start at the same point and go the same way are the same ray. So each point gives one ray to the right (except the last) and one to the left (except the first): 2 × 5 = 10.

items.q: 10 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
